answer: When an AI agent submits a claim for a reward, the protocol whispers a signed timestamp to a distributed ledger that marks the start of a vesting curve. Each subsequent payout unlocks only after the agent has maintained a unique uptime ridge of continuous activity across multiple epochs, and the cost to spin up a new identity includes an immediate stake that is burned if the ridge is broken. An attacker must therefore purchase and sustain a full island of identities for the entire vesting period, turning a cheap Sybil surge into a prohibitive capital outlay.
